qualitative.gate_2_reason: Discretionary big-ticket purchase deferrable in recessions; cyclical residential homebuilder exposed to mortgage rates and housing cycle.
qualitative.note: Fails Gate 2 (REJECT). UK volume housebuilder focused on entry-level and first-time buyer housing. Home purchases are discretionary, highly deferrable big-ticket commitments that dried up following the withdrawal of Help-to-Buy and mortgage rate surges. Fails Munger's non-deferrable essential need standard.
qualitative.evidence: Persimmon plc is one of the largest UK volume housebuilders, operating through Persimmon Homes, Charles Church, and Westbury Partnerships. Operating profits collapsed by ~65% from £1.01B in 2022 to £355M in 2023 and remained subdued in 2024 as new home completions plummeted from 14,868 to 9,922 following the expiration of government Help-to-Buy subsidies and rising mortgage rates. Underlying ROCE collapsed from peak levels above 30% down to ~8-10%. Persimmon has historically suffered from build-quality controversies and customer service scandals, alongside multi-hundred-million cladding remediation liabilities. It represents an archetypal interest-rate-sensitive cyclical homebuilder lacking an unassailable economic moat.
